title: The legend of Ahalya
introduction: Vishvamitra narrates the legend of Ahalya to Rama and Lakshmana when they arrive at the precincts of Mithila, bidding farewell to the King of Vishaala. Indra is infatuated with Ahalya desires a union with her, for which she complies. However, Gautama catching them unawares curses both Indra and Ahalya.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 48th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
पृष्ट्वा तु कुशलं तत्र परस्परसमागमे |
कथान्ते सुमतिर्वाक्यं व्याजहार महामुनिम्
verses.iast:
pṛṣṭvā tu kuśalam tatra paraspara samāgame |
kathāante sumatiḥ vākyam vyājahāra mahāmunim
verses.translation: When those two, Vishvamitra and Sumati, have met one another there at that place, king Sumati raised the topic of Rama and Lakshmana, after exchanging greetings and enquiring about the well-being of the great-saint Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: one with the other Sumati with Vishvamitra
episode, end of [at end of the exchanging greetings]
with great-saint, words, started - raised the topic of Rama and Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:
इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ |
गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ
पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षौ खड्गतूणीधनुर्धरौ |
अश्विनाविव रूपेण समुपस्थितयौवनौ
यदृच्छयैव गां प्राप्तौ देवलोकादिवामरौ |
कथं पद्भ्यामिह प्राप्तौ किमर्थं कस्य वा मुने
verses.iast:
imau kumārau bhadram te deva tulya parākramau |
gaja siṃha gatī vīrau śārdūla vṛṣabha upamau
padma patra viśālākṣau khaḍga tūṇī dhanur dharau |
aśvinau iva rūpeṇa samupasthita yauvanau
yadṛcchayā eva gām prāptau devalokāt iva amarau |
katham padbhyām iha prāptau kim artham kasya vā mune
verses.translation: "These two youngsters, oh, sage, let safety betide you, striding like audacious elephants and arrogant lions, bearing a similitude to adventurous tigers and adamantine bulls, and wielding quivers, swords, and bows, are valorous with their valour matching that of Vishnu, and with their eyes broad like lotus-petals and with youthfulness in the offing they look like the exceptionally beautiful twin-gods, Ashwin-brothers, by their physique. How these two have footslogged and chanced here as though immortals have chanced on earth from the abode of gods at their pleasure? What for they have come here, and whose scions are they?
notes: The word deva can easily be said as a 'god' but, this is said to be Vishnu, as implied at 4-43-56 of Kishkindha 'There the Cosmic-Souled God, namely Vishnu...' etc. Now the enquirer himself is no less than a godly king, hence he identified the boys as non-terrestrial. No fatherly person accepts youngsters to footslog miles and miles, and so far this is an unobserved and an uncared for aspect by other sages and saints, because all of those sages and saints are footsloggers. This may be one of the reasons for Dasharatha in refusing to send Rama with Vishvamitra. However, King Sumati, being a glorious and fatherly king brought up this topic. Vishvamitra is giving a 'rehearsal' for these brothers for their real forest trekking later in the legend. Further, if a divine deed is to be done and a benefit therefrom is to be acquired, one has to footslog. Now Rama is going to perform a divine feat called 'bending the bow of Shiva' and thereby winning the hand of an unusual princess Seetha, in marriage. Hence, he footslogged this much distance for sītā kalyāṇa artham, loka kalyāṇa artham Seetha's marriage, which is for the 'universal goodness.'

glosses.meaning: with god Vishnu, matching, in valour
[like audacious] elephant, [like arrogant] lion, with strides
by physique, Ashwin, the Twin-god brothers, like

verses.devanagari:
भूषयन्ताविमं देशं चन्द्रसूर्याविवाम्बरम् |
परस्परेण सदृशौ प्रमाणेङ्गितचेष्टितैः
किमर्थं च नरश्रेष्ठौ संप्राप्तौ दुर्गमे पथि |
वरायुधधरौ वीरौ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः
verses.iast:
bhūṣayantau imam deśam candra sūryau iva ambaram |
paraspareṇa sadṛśau pramāṇa ingita ceṣṭitaiḥ
kim artham ca nara śreṣṭhau samprāptau dur.hgame pathi |
vara āyudha dharau vīrau śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
verses.translation: "These two best ones among men are identical to one another by their bodily proportion, facial-language, and by bodily gestures, and with their presence they refurbish this province like the Moon and Sun brightening the firmament. In truth, I would like to know for what reason these valiant ones who are wielding best weapons have arrived here travelling on an arduous path." Thus, king Sumati asked Vishvamitra.
notes: The word facial-language translated for ingita may be an extended expression for the body language.' This word is for the voice muted facial expressions, given through smiles, eyebrows, lip movement etc. A person could be analysed by these very expressions as we presently call this as face reading. This is what Sugreeva says when sending Hanuma to Rama and Lakshmana for the first time, 'because you are an expert in reading faces, know them by their facial expressions...'

glosses.meaning: two best ones among men Rama, Lakshmana
by bodily proportions, [and] by facial-language, [and] by gestures
Moon, Sun, [decorate the] firmament, as with
not, passable, on a route - an arduous path
for what, reason, they have chanced here
in truth, to listen - know, I wish to.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा यथावृत्तं न्यवेदयत् |
सिद्धाश्रमनिवासं च राक्षसानां वधं तथा |
verses.iast:
tasya tad vacanam śrutvā yathā vṛttam nyavedayat |
siddha āśrama nivāsam ca rākṣasānām vadham tathā |
verses.translation: On hearing those words of King Sumati, Vishvamitra informed him about the visit of Rama and Lakshmana to the Hermitage of Accomplishment, also about the elimination of demons, as it has happened.

glosses.meaning: in Accomplishment, hermitage, visit [of Rama and Lakshmana,] also

verses.label: 1.48.7b, 8
verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा राजा परमविस्मितः
अतिथी परमौ प्राप्तं पुत्रौ दशरथस्य तौ |
पूजयामास विधिवत् सत्कारार्हौ महाबलौ
verses.iast:
viśvāmitra vacaḥ śrutvā rājā parama vismitaḥ
atithī paramau prāptam putrau daśarathasya tau |
pūjayāmāsa vidhivat satkāra ar.hhau mahābalau
verses.translation: King Sumati is highly astonished to hear the words of Vishvamitra about the visit of Rama and Lakshmana, and treating them to have come as the most prominent and honour-worthy guests that king started to honour those two great-mighty sons of Dasharatha customarily.

glosses.meaning: most prominent ones, guests, chanced - at his place
to those two, of Dasharatha, sons

verses.devanagari:
ततः परमसत्कारं सुमतेः प्राप्य राघवौ |
उष्य तत्र निशामेकां जग्मतुर्मिथिलां ततः
verses.iast:
tataḥ parama satkāram sumateḥ prāpya rāghavau |
uṣya tatra niśām ekām jagmatuḥ mithilām tataḥ
verses.translation: On getting high honours from King Sumati, Raghava-s stayed there along with Vishvamitra and with the community of sages for one night, and then they all have moved on to Mithila.

glosses.meaning: from Sumati, high, honour, on getting
then, to Mithila, they moved on.

verses.devanagari:
तां दृष्ट्वा मुनयः सर्वे जनकस्य पुरीं शुभाम् |
साधु साध्विति शंसन्तो मिथिलां समपूजयन्
verses.iast:
tām dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ sarve janakasya purīm śubhām |
sādhu sādhu iti śaṃsanto mithilām samapūjayan
verses.translation: On seeing Janaka's auspicious city Mithila, all of the saints who are accompanying Vishvamitra, Rama, and Lakshmana, extolled it saying, "Splendid! Splendid!" and admired it highly.
notes: Ayodhya is not fortunate enough to receive any worship from the onlookers, but it will be admired for its fortification. However, Mithila is a venerable city, because by itself it is a temple town and the Vedic-rituals etc., will be going on forever. It is a blessed place as it has Shiva's Bow, for which bow ritual worship is be ongoing from time immemorial.

verses.devanagari:
मिथिलोपवने तत्र आश्रमं दृश्य राघवः |
पुराणं निर्जनं रम्यं पप्रच्छ मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.iast:
mithila upavane tatra āśramam dṛśya rāghavaḥ |
purāṇam nirjanam raṃyam papraccha muni puṅgavam
verses.translation: On seeing a hermitage in the fringes of Mithila, that appeared to be age-old, but now uninhabited, yet pleasing, Rama asked the eminent sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: Mithila, near at, in woodlands - in fringe woods of Mithila

verses.devanagari:
इदमाश्रमसंकाशं किं न्विदं मुनिवर्जितम् |
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन् कस्यायं पूर्व आश्रमः
verses.iast:
idam āśrama saṅkāśam kim nu idam muni varjitam |
śrotum icchāmi bhagavan kasya ayam pūrva āśramaḥ
verses.translation: "This is semblable to a hermitage but sages seem to have discarded it. Oh, venerable sage, whose is this hermitage previously, I wish to listen of it." Thus, Rama asked Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: previously, this, hermitage, whose is it

verses.devanagari:
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवेणोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः |
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा विश्वमित्रो महामुनिः
verses.iast:
tat śrutā rāghaveṇa uktam vākyam vākya viśāradaḥ |
prati uvāca mahātejā viśvamitro mahāmuniḥ
verses.translation: On hearing that sentence spoken by Raghava, the expert in sententiousness, a great resplendent sage and eminent-saint Vishvamitra replied him in this way.

verses.devanagari:
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि शृणु तत्त्वेन राघव |
यस्यैतदाश्रमपदं शप्तं कोपान्महात्मना
verses.iast:
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvena rāghava |
yasya etat āśrama padam śaptam kopān mahātmanā
verses.translation: "What a pleasure! You may listen as I narrate, Raghava, whose hermitage is this factually, and which great soul has resentfully cursed this.
notes: The pleasure expressed by Vishvamitra is for the arrival of time, for the event of Rama's grace, in releasing Ahalya from her cursed state.

glosses.meaning: factually, to you, I will narrate
what a pleasure - to tell about it to you.

verses.devanagari:
गौतमस्य नरश्रेष्ठ पूर्वमासीन्महात्मनः |
आश्रमो दिव्यसंकाशः सुरैरपि सुपूजितः
verses.iast:
gautamasya naraśreṣṭha pūrvam āsīt mahātmanaḥ |
āśramo divya saṅkāśaḥ suraiḥ api supūjitaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, the best one among men Rama, this hermitage with a heavenly glisten, and highly hallowed even by gods, once belonged to the great-souled sage Gautama.

glosses.meaning: of great-souled one, Gautama's, was there - belonged to.

verses.devanagari:
स चात्र तप आतिष्ठदहल्यासहितः पुरा |
वर्षपूगान्यनेकानि राजपुत्र महायशः
verses.iast:
sa ca atra tapa ātiṣṭhat ahalyā sahitaḥ purā |
varṣa pūgāni anekāni rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
verses.translation: "In this hermitage, oh, prince Rama, once that highly renowned Sage Gautama sat tight in asceticism for numerous cycle of years along with his wife Ahalya.

glosses.meaning: Ahalya [his wife,] along with an ekaani = not, one - numerous
there - in this hermitage, in asceticism, sat tight.

verses.devanagari:
तस्यान्तरं विदित्वा तु सहस्राक्षः शचीपतिः |
मुनिवेषधरो भूत्वाऽहल्यामिदमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tasya antaram viditvā tu sahasrākṣaḥ śacī patiḥ |
muni veṣa dharo bhūtvā ahalyām idam abravīt
verses.translation: "On knowing the meantime of Gautama's availability at hermitage, Indra, the husband of Shaci Devi and the Thousand-eyed god wearing the guise of sage Gautama and becoming such a sage, approached Ahalya and said this to her.

glosses.meaning: meantime, gap period [from his stay with his wife in ascetics]

verses.devanagari:
ऋतुकालं प्रतीक्षन्ते नार्थिनः सुसमाहिते |
संगमं त्वहमिच्छामि त्वया सह सुमध्यमे
verses.iast:
ṛtu kālam pratīkṣante na arthinaḥ susamāhite |
saṅgamam tu aham icchāmi tvayā saha sumadhyame
verses.translation: " 'Oh, finely limbed lady, indulgers do not watch out for the time to conceive, as such oh, slender-waisted one, I desire copulation with you.
notes: Vividly: 'Oh, Ahalya, Brahma crafted you so well that all your limbs are symmetrically conjoined, so who in the universe will not yearn to have intercourse with you... and on seeing your slender waist and thickset hips I wish to copulate with you now itself... and let there be no fear of safe period or unsafe period for I do not wish to have any progeny of mine from you...

glosses.meaning: seasonal [conceiving,] time, not, watch out for

verses.devanagari:
मुनिवेषं सहस्राक्षं विज्ञाय रघुनंदन |
मतिं चकार दुर्मेधा देवराजकुतूहलात्
verses.iast:
muni veṣam sahasrākṣam viGYāya raghunandana |
matim cakāra durmedhā deva rāja kutūhalāt
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, though knowing him as the Thousand-eyed Indra in the guise of her husband Gautama, she is inclined to have intercourse ill-advisedly, only to satisfy the impassion of the King of Gods.
notes: Her thinking is: 'This is none but Indra in the guise of my husband, for my husband never asks me like this nor he violates times... I heard that Indra is seeking me for a long time... and when King of Gods expresses such a desire, it cannot be refused... let him have it

glosses.meaning: in sage's, guise, of Thousand-eyed one, [though] knowing
mind, made - inclined to have intercourse.

verses.devanagari:
अथाब्रवीत् सुरश्रेष्ठं कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना |
कृतार्थास्मि सुरश्रेष्ठ गच्छ शीघ्रमितः प्रभो
आत्मानं मां च देवेश सर्वदा रक्ष गौतमात् |
verses.iast:
atha abravīt suraśreṣṭham kṛtārthena antarātmanā |
kṛtārthā asmi suraśreṣṭha gaccha śīghram itaḥ prabho
ātmānam mām ca deveśa sarvadā rakṣa gautamāt |
verses.translation: "She felt fulfilled in her heart of hearts and then she said this to that best god Indra, 'I am gratified in complying with your wish, oh, best of gods, get going oh, lord, from here quickly, oh, ruler of gods, always safeguard yourself and me from Sage Gautama.' Thus, Ahalya said to Indra.

glosses.meaning: fulfilled, means, in heart, of hearts
of gods, to the best one - Indra

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्रस्तु प्रहसन् वाक्यमहल्यामिदमब्रवीत्
सुश्रोणि परितुष्टोऽस्मि गमिष्यामि यथागतम् |
verses.iast:
indraḥ tu prahasan vākyam ahalyām idam abravīt
suśroṇi parituṣṭo asmi gamiṣyāmi yathā āgatam |
verses.translation: "Indra on his part smilingly said this word to Ahalya, 'oh, well-hipped lady, I am quite delighted, here I go as I have came.'

glosses.meaning: as I have come, I will go away.

verses.devanagari:
एवं संगम्य तु तया निश्चक्रामोटजात्ततः
स संभ्रमात्त्वरन् राम शङ्कितो गौतमं प्रति |
verses.iast:
evam saṅgaṃya tu tayā niścakrāma uṭajāt tataḥ
sa sambhramāt tvaran rāma śankito gautamam prati |
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, Indra then came out of the cottage flustering hurriedly after copulating with her with an uncertainty about the arrival of Sage Gautama.

glosses.meaning: at Gautama, towards [his arrival,] uncertain of

verses.devanagari:
गौतमं स ददर्शाथ प्रविशन्तं महामुनिम्
देवदानवदुर्धर्षं तपोबलसमन्वितम् |
तीर्थोदकपरिक्लिन्नं दीप्यमानमिवानलम्
गृहीतसमिधं तत्र सकुशं मुनिपुंगवम् |
verses.iast:
gautamam sa dadarśa atha praviśantam mahāmunim
deva dānava durdharṣam tapo bala samanvitam |
tīrtha udaka pariklinnam dīpyamānam iva analam
gṛhīta samidham tatra sa kuśam muni puṅgavam |
verses.translation: "Indra has then seen the great-saint Gautama, an unassailable sage either for gods or for demons owing to his ascetic prowess, though thoroughly wet with the water of pious river he is luminous like ritual fire, and a foremost saint among all saints who just entered the hermitage carrying ritual firewood and sacred grass.

glosses.meaning: for gods, for demons, an unassailable one

verses.devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा सुरपतिस्त्रस्तो विषण्णवदनोऽभवत्
अथ दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षं मुनिवेषधरं मुनिः |
दुर्वृत्तं वृत्तसंपन्नो रोषाद्वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭvā sura patiḥ trasto viṣaṇṇa vadano abhavat
atha dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣam muni veṣa dharam muniḥ |
dur.hvṛttam vṛtta sampanno roṣāt vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: "On seeing the sage the lord of gods Indra is scared and became dreary-faced. Then the well-behaved Gautama furiously spoke these words on seeing the ill-behaved Thousand-eyed Indra who is donning the guise of a saint.

glosses.meaning: saint's, guise, who is wearing - Indra

verses.devanagari:
मम रूपं समास्थाय कृतवानसि दुर्मते |
अकर्तव्यमिदं यस्मात् विफलस्त्वं भविष्यति
verses.iast:
mama rūpam samāsthāya kṛtavān asi dur.hmate |
akartavyam idam yasmāt viphalaḥ tvam bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: " 'Oh, dirty-minded Indra, taking hold of my form you have effectuated this unacceptable deed, whereby you shall become infecund.' Thus, Gautama cursed Indra.

verses.devanagari:
गौतमेनैवमुक्तस्य स रोषेण महात्मना |
पेततुर्वृषणौ भूमौ सहस्राक्षस्य तत्क्षणात्
verses.iast:
gautamena evam uktasya sa roṣeṇa mahātmanā |
petatuḥ vṛṣaṇau bhūmau sahasrākṣasya tat kṣaṇāt
verses.translation: "When that great-souled sage Gautama spoke that way with rancour, the testicles of the cursed Thousand-eyed Indra fell down onto ground at that very moment.

glosses.meaning: that way, of the one who is spoken to [cursed, Indra's]

verses.devanagari:
तथा शप्त्वा च वै शक्रं भार्यामपि च शप्तवान् |
इह वर्षसहस्राणि बहूनि निवसिष्यसि
वायुभक्षा निराहारा तप्यन्ती भस्मशायिनी |
अदृश्या सर्वभूतानामाश्रमेऽस्मिन् निवत्स्यसि
verses.iast:
tathā śaptvā ca vai śakram bhāryām api ca śaptavān |
iha varṣa sahasrāṇi bahūni nivaṣisyasi
vāyu bhakṣā nirāhārā tapyantī bhasma śāyinī |
adṛśyā sarva bhūtānām āśrame asmin vaṣisyasi
verses.translation: "On cursing Indra thus the sage cursed even his wife saying, 'you shall tarry here for many thousands of years to come without food and consuming air alone, and unseen by all beings you shall live on in this hermitage while contritely recumbent in dust.

glosses.meaning: in this, hermitage, you live on.

verses.devanagari:
यदा त्वेतद्वनं घोरं रामो दशरथात्मजः |
आगमिष्यति दुर्धर्षस्तदा पूता भविष्यसि
verses.iast:
yadā tu etat vanam ghoram rāmo daśaratha ātmajaḥ |
āgamiṣyati durdharṣaḥ tadā pūtā bhaviṣyasi
verses.translation: " 'When that unassailable son of Dasharatha, namely Rama, arrives at this squalid forest, for it will be henceforth rendered so along with you, then you will be purified.

verses.devanagari:
तस्यातिथ्येन दुर्वृत्ते लोभमोहविवर्जिता |
मत्सकाशे मुदा युक्ता स्वं वपुर्धारयिष्यसि
verses.iast:
tasya ātithyena dur.hvṛtte lobha moha vivarjitā |
mat sakāśe mudā yuktā svam vapuḥ dhārayiṣyasi
verses.translation: " 'On your welcoming Rama, oh, ill-behaved woman, you will be divested of your greed and craze in which you lingered so far, and then you will assume your own body and then you can be in my proximity, rejoicingly.' Thus, Sage Gautama cursed his wife Ahalya.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा गौतमो दुष्टचारिणीम् |
इममाश्रममुत्सृज्य सिद्धचारणसेविते |
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये तपस्तेपे महातपाः
verses.iast:
evam uktvā mahātejā gautamo duṣṭa cāriṇīm |
imam āśramam utsṛjya siddha cāraṇa sevite |
himavat śikhare raṃye tapaḥ tepe mahātapāḥ
verses.translation: "On cursing immodest Ahalya thus, that great-resplendent Sage Gautama shed this hermitage which was once adored by celestials like siddha-sand caarana-s, and that great-ascetic Gautama practised his asceticism on the pleasant peaks of Himalayas." Thus, Vishvamitra continued his narration about the legend of Ahalya.

glosses.meaning: to bad, behaved one - to immodest Ahalya
